subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK foundation: host-FS read/write, exec-class tools, slash/CLI dispatch, and generic cron tool-call payloads?
rationale: Current code intentionally denies high-risk tools and active PRs cover only narrow slices, so automation cannot choose the permanent security boundary or operator opt-in model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep umbrella, land narrow gated slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review the host-FS and startup-readiness PRs separately and require explicit owner gates, docs, audits, and upgrade proof for each privileged surface.

options.title: Freeze at shipped direct invoke
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK direct invoke plus command cron sufficient for now and close or reject the remaining host-FS, exec, shorthand, and generic cron asks as out of scope.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Adopt a broader direct-execution design only after a named security model covers exec-class tools, cron/gateway/node control, owner identity, approval behavior, and auditability.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review the host-FS and startup-readiness PRs separately and require explicit owner gates, docs, audits, and upgrade proof for each privileged surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the centralized dangerous-tool deny-list boundary and is the strongest history signal for the security decision this umbrella still needs.
